target_customer: Brazilian small and mid-sized companies and startups wanting performance reviews, OKRs, 1:1s and engagement surveys
problem: Companies lacked structured people management and OKR tools. Qulture.Rocks sold software plus help designing the processes.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with process consulting
product_category: People, OKR and culture management software

founders.name: Francisco Homem de Mello
founders.background_notes: YC page says about 10 years in investment banking and investment management without naming the firms. Brazil Journal gives 2014 as the founding year while YC says 2015.

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard HR workflow SaaS with Slack integrations.

defensibility.rationale: Review and goal history created some lock-in and a Portuguese local focus helped, but many global tools overlapped.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Global tools competed on features, and the company was ultimately bought by a Brazilian edtech group in 2022.

market_need_then: OKR and performance practices were spreading among startups. By 2022 the company had about 1,000 paying clients, 80 percent small and mid-sized businesses, per Brazil Journal. No 2018 demand data was found.

branding.domain_note: qulture.rocks, using a .rocks top level domain as part of the name.
branding.brand_signature: The name itself with a .rocks domain ending

brand_strength.rationale: Known in Brazilian startup circles through acquisition coverage, but no source about the brand itself was found and the spelling is unusual.

outcome_analysis: Qulture.Rocks built people and OKR software for Brazilian companies and grew to about 1,000 paying clients with a small cap table of funds holding 32 percent. UOL EdTech bought it in April 2022 on undisclosed terms and the funds exited while the founder stayed as CEO with equity. Capital raised appears small, so the result looks capital efficient, but exact funding is unknown.
notes: Unverified aggregator funding: CB Insights 320 thousand over 6 rounds, PitchBook 455 thousand, Startup Intros a 120 thousand seed in 2018-03, Seedtable 100 thousand in 2019-02. Brazil Journal names Y Combinator, Canary and Redpoint eVentures as top investors but gives no amounts, so no round is recorded. The YC long description mentions Founders Fund, Blackstone, Sequoia and Tiger Global as backers, which I could not confirm in any press source. The company site was not fetchable here. A dated 2018 competitor search returned only 2026 comparison pages, so the list is empty. The acquisition may have closed about three months before the announcement per one outlet.
